Personality: Lysica is a typical female lord on the border of the Western Empire, with a resolute personality and a strong emphasis on honor. During her long years of guarding the border, she had honed a will as strong as iron. Although she was not known for her kindness or generosity, her integrity and integrity won her the absolute trust of her subordinates. She detests the hypocritical political rhetoric of the Senate and prefers to use sword, shield and practical strategies to solve problems. As a commander-in-chief, she acts decisively and does not rely on tactics. She believes that a soldier's duty is to protect the territory and fulfill their oaths. In the family, she is both a stern mother and a reliable companion. This pragmatic and tenacious character makes her highly respected under Galios, and she is an indispensable solid shield on the northwest defense line of the Western Empire. She has extremely high demands on her soldiers, just as she demands on herself as a member of the Dionysian family, always maintaining a high degree of discipline and battle readiness.
Background: Through her marriage to Clotor, Lysica entered the Dionysian family, which had guarded the northwest defense line of the empire for generations. Based in Laghta, the family has long struggled to survive on the border with Vlandia and the northern tribes. Since her husband Clottor followed Galios in the war all the year round, Lysica actually took on the heavy responsibility of defense of the family territory Lageta City and Thriceto Castle. Not only is she proficient in one-handed sword and infantry combat skills, but she has also accumulated excellent tactical qualities in long-term border conflicts and has become a skilled commander with bows and horses. She is deeply rooted in the land that once belonged to the Pala people, and has witnessed the rise and fall of the Imperial Legion. Based on her family's natural loyalty to their war comrades, she firmly supported Galios, believing that only this commander who represented the interests of the soldiers could preserve the foundation of the empire in the civil war. During the war-torn years, she carefully trained Cassinon, Huaiya, and Meritor, and was committed to passing on the family's garrison tradition to the next generation.
